answer: Every claimed task must lock a small escrow bond that releases only after an independent verifier confirms the work; a failed check burns the bond. A sparrow of fake identities cannot share one bond — each must fund its own jetty of claims, so the cost of a farm grows with every fake while honest agents recycle a single bond across epochs. The gale of audits is random and unpredictable, so clones cannot time their fraud around it, and burned bonds fund the auditors who caught them.
